items.title: The painting most cited as Cubism's origin
items.claim: Which 1907 Picasso painting is most often cited as a key precursor to Cubism?
items.reveal:
Picasso painted the work in 1907 but did not exhibit it publicly until 1916. The fractured planes and reference to Iberian and African sculpture set the conditions for Cubism with Braque.

It is now in MoMA, New York.
items.why: A painting can remain influential through private circulation among artists before reaching the public.

items.title: The most expensive painting sold
items.claim: Which painting holds the auction record set in November 2017?
items.reveal:
The Leonardo attribution to Salvator Mundi remains contested by some scholars. The buyer was reportedly acting for the Saudi crown prince.

The painting has not been publicly displayed since the sale.
items.why: Attribution debates and market records are intertwined in the history of major paintings.

items.title: Warhol's first soup cans
items.claim: Andy Warhol's first Campbell's Soup Cans exhibition was in which city in 1962?
items.reveal:
The 32 canvases (one per Campbell's variety) were priced at around $100 each. Ferus's owner Irving Blum bought the entire series for around $1,000 and later sold it to MoMA for around $15 million.

The work consolidated Pop Art's place in American museums within a decade.
items.why: Pop Art's commercial trajectory mirrored the consumer culture it depicted.
